hook.line: Anger comes in sizes, and picking the wrong one makes a fight bigger. Spanish has a ladder: *me da rabia* is personal, *me indigna* is about what's unfair, *no aguanto que* is a line you won't cross.
hook.es: Me da rabia que no me hayas avisado.
hook.en: It makes me angry that you didn't tell me. (to a friend)

examples.es: Me da rabia que no me hayas avisado.
examples.en: It makes me angry that you didn't tell me. (to a friend)

examples.es: Me indigna que hayan despedido a tanta gente sin explicación.
examples.en: It outrages me that they've fired so many people without explanation.

examples.es: Me da mucha rabia que Altamira compre toda la cuadra.
examples.en: It makes me really angry that Altamira is buying the whole block.

examples.es: Me indigna que le hablen así a Hernando.

rule:
Three steps up. *Me da rabia que…* is personal: it hurts me. *Me indigna que…* is moral: it's unfair. *No aguanto que…* is a limit: I won't take it.

They work like *me pone nervioso*: the cause comes first, then *que* and the wish form: *que me interrumpan*.

For something already done, use *hayas* or *hayan* plus the *-ado* form: *que no me hayas avisado*.

Add *mucha* to *rabia* to push it. Save *indignar* for injustice, not a late bus.
smallPrint: Teachers call *hayas avisado* the perfect subjunctive: the wish form of *haber* plus the *-ado* form.

readAndPick.es: Me da rabia que no me hayas avisado.
options: It makes me angry that you won't tell me.
It makes me angry that you didn't tell me.
It makes me angry that I didn't tell you.
I can't stand interrupting them.
They can't stand being interrupted.
I can't stand being interrupted.

readAndPick.es: Me indigna que hayan despedido a tanta gente sin explicación.
options: It outrages me that they've fired so many people without explanation.
It outrages me that they're going to fire many people.
I'm outraged at having fired so many people.

readAndPick.es: Me da mucha rabia que Altamira compre toda la cuadra.
options: It makes me really angry that Altamira bought the whole block.
It makes me really angry that Altamira is buying the whole block.
Altamira is really angry that I'm buying the whole block.

readAndPick.es: Me da rabia que hayas dicho eso.
options: It makes me angry that you say that.
It makes you angry that I said that.
It makes me angry that you said that.

readAndPick.es: No aguanto que me hablen así.
options: I won't put up with being spoken to like that.
I don't like speaking like this.
I can't speak like that.

readAndPick.es: Me indigna que le hablen así a Hernando.
options: Hernando is outraged that they talk to me like that.
It outrages me that they talk to Hernando like that.
It outrages Hernando that I talk like that.

readAndPick.es: Me da mucha rabia no poder ayudar.
options: It makes you really angry not to help.
It makes me really angry that you can't help.
It makes me really angry not to be able to help.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right form and type the whole sentence: *Me indigna que ___ despedido a tanta gente.* (*hayan* or *han*)
yourTurn.answer: Me indigna que hayan despedido a tanta gente.
yourTurn.why: After *me indigna que* the verb takes the wish form, and for something done that is *hayan*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I can't stand being interrupted.
yourTurn.why: *No aguanto que* plus the wish form: *interrumpan*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It makes me really angry that Altamira is buying the whole block.
yourTurn.answer: Me da mucha rabia que Altamira compre toda la cuadra.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It outrages me that they talk to Hernando like that.
yourTurn.answer: Me indigna que le hablen así a Hernando.
accept: Me indigna que le hablen a Hernando así.
yourTurn.why: Injustice is *me indigna que*, with *hablen* as the wish form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: It makes me angry that you didn't tell me.
yourTurn.answer: Me da rabia que no me hayas avisado.

yourTurn.prompt: Take it up a step: *Me da rabia que no me hayas avisado.* Say it with *indignar*.
yourTurn.answer: Me indigna que no me hayas avisado.
yourTurn.why: *Me indigna* is the moral level: it feels unfair.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I won't put up with being spoken to like that.
yourTurn.answer: No aguanto que me hablen así.
yourTurn.why: The limit is *no aguanto que* plus *hablen*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me da rabia de que no me hayas avisado.
pitfalls.right: Me da rabia que no me hayas avisado.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish has no *de* before *que* here.
Almost. After *no aguanto que* the verb takes the wish form: *interrumpan*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me da rabia que no me avisaste.
pitfalls.right: Me da rabia que no me hayas avisado.
pitfalls.why: Almost. For something already done, use *hayas* plus the *-ado* form.

personal: Say one thing that makes you angry, in the right size. Start with *Me da rabia…*, *Me indigna…* or *No aguanto que…*
